assigned.title: The desktop forwarder spec shares one ledger across parallel workers
assigned.acceptance: The desktop forwarder spec gives the same answer however many workers Playwright runs it with. It does not today: the stub backend keeps ONE request ledger for the whole process, three tests clear it and then assert it holds exactly their own request, and playwright.config.ts sets fullyParallel: true -- which splits tests WITHIN a file across workers. A two-core machine gets one worker and the file passes; a CI runner gets several and a neighbour's forwarded request lands between the clear and the read. CI run 37007312900 failed exactly that way on three assertions, and --workers=4 reproduces it locally. REQUIRED: the isolation is structural rather than a matter of how many cores the machine running it happens to have. REQUIRED: toHaveLength(1) survives unchanged -- it is the assertion that a forwarder neither retries nor fans out, which the spec records as 'a duplicated session request against a real backend is a duplicated authorization', and relaxing it to 'at least one' would delete the check in order to make the schedule convenient. REQUIRED: the repair is demonstrated under more workers than the machine has cores, because a pass at one worker is what hid this for as long as it was hidden.
assigned.notes: FILED IN ROUND 104 from CI run 37007312900 on d6d0324, which is the first run after the branch was published. Not caused by that round: neither PW-0309 nor PW-0503 touches this spec, the stub or the forwarder.

e2e.evidence: RE-RECORDED to carry the GitHub result, which the first recording could not. Implementation 2f69f2d07c05bc077505f5d7326ef998a628ba17; confirmed on CI run 37028642916 at commit 30cef6e88a0bac82bf60fd4c9500c5ce4003da8f, the first commit GitHub has executed containing the repair. ITS e2e JOB COMPLETED IN 3m 33s WITH NO ERROR ANNOTATIONS: '14 skipped 93 passed' development, '31 skipped 76 passed' production -- the same counts measured locally. The two prior runs, 37007312900 on d6d0324 and 37022965860 on 64a76b3, each failed exactly three assertions in that spec, the second time all three reading 'Expected 1 request received 2'; both predate the repair. The runner's own worker count is what exposed the shared ledger and is what has now exercised the per-invocation correlation identity -- the environment this container could only approximate. LOCAL EVIDENCE UNCHANGED AND STILL THE BASIS. Old implementation --workers=4: 1 failed / 8 passed; old --repeat-each=3 --workers=4: 5 failed / 22 passed. Repaired: 0 failed at 4 and at 8 workers; 27 passed at --repeat-each=3 --workers=4; 45 passed at --repeat-each=5 --workers=8; whole api project 55 passed / 8 skipped at both worker counts. Collateral, whole projects: development chromium+api 93/14, production 61/46, production + real PostgreSQL 16.15 76/31; apps/web 84 files / 1494 tests. fullyParallel stays enabled, retries stay 0, no timeout ceiling was raised, and toHaveLength(1) is unchanged in all three places. NOT CLAIMED: the run as a whole had not concluded when this was read -- validate takes about 27 minutes -- so this records the e2e JOB's result, which is the job that failed twice and the only one this task is about.

recommended.title: Install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall — tested, not assumed
recommended.acceptance: The installer's lifecycle is exercised automatically wherever that is possible on a runner, and everything that is not is named for the commander's machine. REQUIRED: clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch. REQUIRED: upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved, which is the one a release breaks most often and nobody tests. REQUIRED: uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps or removes. REQUIRED: reinstall after uninstall. REQUIRED: each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason, so the split is visible rather than implied.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. review.evidence: CHANGES REQUESTED at 835823561c69f5bbdebf19c637eeeabff19dacf7. Transcribed by claude-lead from gpt-architect's round-105 ruling, section 2, which is a request for changes in substance even though it does not use the word: 'The lifecycle harness architecture is accepted. DO NOT mark PW-0503 DONE merely to free the Test lane. Current Windows evidence establishes only part of the lifecycle matrix.' gpt's itemised verdict: F1 clean install PARTIAL PASS -- the MSI builds, installs and its installed tree is verified; still unverified is actual installed application launch and WebView runtime. F2 upgrade UNVERIFIED -- no real previous release has been exercised as an upgrade source, so user-data preservation across an actual upgrade remains unproven. F3 uninstall PARTIAL PASS -- msiexec uninstall executes; still to prove where automation permits are no orphaned service, no scheduled task, no orphaned node.exe, expected files removed, and documented user-data retention behaviour. F4 reinstall UNVERIFIED but AUTOMATABLE -- 'implement and execute this rather than classifying it as commander-only'. WHAT HAS CHANGED SINCE THAT VERDICT WAS WRITTEN, and it narrows the request rather than answering it: the IMPLEMENTATION of F3's residue classification and of F4 reinstall already exists in scripts/windows/lifecycle.mjs and residue.mjs at the commit above, with 30 cases behind the decisions, and F4 is already marked plannedAutomated with no manual portion. What does not exist is EXECUTION, and it cannot be created by any open task: no open task can write .github/workflows/windows.yml -- every writer is DONE and PW-0502, PW-0503 and PW-0602 hold it read-only. That is recorded as a board.sequencing_finding and needs a ruling on which task gets the write surface. Recorded so the task leaves REVIEW honestly rather than being completed on evidence gpt declined to accept.

recommended.title: The automated half of the Windows matrix, running on Windows
recommended.acceptance: Every row PW-0601 marks automated runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails. REQUIRED: the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu -- the desktop axis is currently built on Ubuntu only, and only incidentally, because the axis defaults on and openssl happens to be installed. REQUIRED: the shell is driven end to end where the harness can reach it, and where it cannot, the row stays in the commander-machine half rather than being replaced by a unit test that proves something easier. REQUIRED: retries stay at zero, on the rule playwright.config.ts already states at length. REQUIRED: a row that is skipped says why, by name, the way the existing harness already does for the desktop and media-rig axes.
